extracted.intended_audience: actors, playwrights, and essayists / literate public interested in theatrical and essayistic craft
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on stage action, gesture, voice, and dramatic delivery together with norms for essay/letter composition, authorship honesty, and the use of fictional personae in periodical essays. Aimed at producing persuasive theatre and respectable Spectator-style papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of countenance requires judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: As the Countenance admits of so great Variety, it requires also great Judgment to govern it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not shift the form of the face on every occasion (lest it turn to Farce and Buffoonery), but use appropriate variation of expression to match the sentiments. Govern facial change deliberately so it reads true rather than exaggerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyes as principal markers of emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eyes have a wonderful Power of marking the Emotions of the Mind, sometimes by a stedfast Look, sometimes by a careless one, now by a sudden Regard, then by a joyful Sparkling, as the Sense of the Words is diversified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ varied eye-expressions (steadfast, careless, sudden regard, joyful sparkle) to reflect changes in meaning and feeling; eyes communicate nuance that words alone may not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action must conform to the sentiments of the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is, as it were, the Speech of the Features and Limbs, and must therefore conform itself always to the Sentiments of the Soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure gestures and bodily action arise from inner sentiment—they should be motivated and truthful, not arbitrary ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overacting: guard against turning to farce
rubrics_metrics.description: Not that the Form of the Face is to be shifted on every Occasion, lest it turn to Farce and Buffoonery;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation is essential—excessive variation or demonstrative faces will undermine dignity and veracity of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action as a universal language
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is a kind of Universal Tongue; all Men are subject to the same Passions, and consequently know the same Marks of them in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on expressive gesture and physical action to reach audiences who may not understand every word; physicality can communicate across barriers of language and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good sense is prerequisite to good acting
rubrics_metrics.description: Without Good Sense no one can be a good Player, and he is very unfit to personate the Dignity of a Roman Hero, who cannot enter into the Rules for Pronunciation and Gesture delivered by a Roman Orator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors must possess judgment and understanding of rhetorical/gestural rules; technique alone is insufficient without common sense and comprehension of role dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Govern pronunciation and gesture by rhetorical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter into the Rules for Pronunciation and Gesture delivered by a Roman Orator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study oratorical principles (pronunciation, modulation, gesture) and adapt them to character and historical/dignified personae to convey authority convincingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right pitching of the voice: medium, compass, and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Voice... has its particular Medium and Compass, and the Sweetness of Speech consists in leading it through all the Variety of Tones naturally, and without touching any Extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find your voice's natural medium and compass; practice moving through varied tones within that range. Avoid extremes of pitch; use modulation to express meaning. (Metaphor: leave the tuning-pipe but keep the habit of proper pitch.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use look, voice, and gesture to insinuate into affections
rubrics_metrics.description: Laying wait not only for their superficial Applause, but also for insinuating into their Affections and Passions, by the artful Management of the Look, Voice, and Gesture of the Speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim beyond immediate applause—craft performances to engage audience emotions and passions through deliberate coordination of looks, vocal color, and movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action, show, and dress permissible when they serve entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advantages of Action, Show, and Dress on these Occasions are allowable, because the Merit consists in being capable of imposing upon us to our Advantage and Entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theatrical embellishments (costume, spectacle) are acceptable if they enhance the audience's engagement and provide benefit/entertainment; they function as tools to facilitate the play's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fictitious letters/personae for rhetorical and practical ends
rubrics_metrics.description: I often chuse this way of casting my Thoughts into a Letter... First, out of the Policy of those who try their Jest upon another... Secondly, because I would extort a little Praise... Thirdly, because it gave me an Opportunity of introducing a great variety of Characters... Fourthly, because the Dignity Spectatorial would have suffered... And lastly, because they often serve to bring in, more naturally, such additional Reflections...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt fictitious correspondents or personae to test jokes anonymously, elicit praise, introduce diverse characters, preserve authorial dignity, and provide natural transitions to reflective commentary. Make it clear by style when something is fictional so readers can discern truth vs invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should acknowledge borrowings and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: An Author is guilty of Falshood, when he talks to the Publick of Manuscripts which he never saw... Those who are truly learned will acquit me in this Point, in which I have been so far from offending, that I have been scrupulous perhaps to a Fault in quoting the Authors of several Passages which I might have made my own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be scrupulous in citing sources and acknowledging translations or borrowings; transparency about provenance of ideas is an authorial virtue and defends against charges of dishonesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider each paper a distinct tract
rubrics_metrics.description: I desire my Reader to consider every particular Paper or Discourse as a distinct Tract by itself, and independent of every thing that goes before or after it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat individual essays as self-contained pieces; avoid assuming continuous context so each piece can be read and judged on its own merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance subject-matter to satisfy divergent reader expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some who affirm a Paper of this Nature should always turn upon diverting Subjects, and others who find Fault with every one of them that hath not an immediate Tendency to the Advancement of Religion or Learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that audiences have differing expectations—some prefer light diversion, others moral or instructive content. Strive for proportion and ensure most pieces are at least innocent and inclined to discountenance vice and ignorance while supporting wisdom and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty to purchasers/readers: disclose defects and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unjust to make any Step towards Gain, wherein the Gain of even those to whom you sell is not also consulted... he is no better than a Cheat who sells any thing without telling the Exceptions against it, as well as what is to be said to its Advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting work for public consumption (plays, essays, goods), disclose limitations and exceptions alongside merits; do not deceive consumers/readers by withholding relevant negative information.
